newsitem.title: UK: British troops defuse mine in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: British troops defuse mine in Northern Ireland.

text.p: British bomb disposal officers defused an anti-personnel mine on the outskirts of Dungannon town in Northern Ireland, police said on Friday.
Security sources said they suspected it was the work of guerrillas targetting police officers who had been searching the area this week for the body of a murdered woman.
No organisation claimed responsibility but security sources said the device bore the hallmarks of the Irish Republican Army (IRA) which is fighting to end British rule.

"It was placed at head height in a tree at the side of the road. It was an anti-personnel device filled with semtex (high explosive), shrapnel and oil," a spokeswoman for the Royal Ulster Constabulary said.
In an unconnected operation police officers had searched an area nearby on Monday night and found a woman's body the following day, she said.
"Obviously there were a lot of police in the area at that time searching and carrying out house to house inquiries, and obviously somebody has taken advantage of that," the spokesman said.
IRA guerrillas have used a wide variety of home-made mortars and other bombs in an escalating war against British forces.
Police blamed them for a bomb that was detonated close to a security forces patrol in an Irish nationalist housing estate in west Belfast on Thursday.
